meta.title: Insurance Technology Foundation | Architecture, Workflow, Data & APIs
meta.description: Build insurance products and digital journeys on configurable workflows, APIs, identity, data, documents and integration that work with established enterprise systems.

hero.title: Built to work with the insurance technology you already have.
hero.lede: Iorta TechNXT products are designed for enterprise insurance environments where new digital journeys have to coexist with policy administration, CRM, claims, billing, identity, document and data platforms. The foundation is not one mandatory technology stack. It is a set of architecture principles that help new experiences connect safely, change faster and remain governable.

sections.title: Let the interface change at its own pace.
body: Customer, advisor, broker, partner and employee interfaces should be separated from the constraints of the systems underneath where that creates value.
This allows experience change to move at a different pace from policy or core-system change.

sections.title: Put process change into configuration where it belongs.
body: Workflow should represent business progression without hard-coding every market and product variation into application code.

sections.title: Expose insurance capabilities once.
body: Expose insurance capabilities once so sales, customer, partner and operational applications can reuse them.

sections.title: Define ownership before copying the data.
body: Not every product should create its own copy of enterprise data. Define ownership and freshness according to the use case.

sections.title: Follow the enterprise identity model.
body: Identity architecture is market-specific and enterprise-specific, so integrations should follow the customer's chosen identity model.

sections.title: Keep the evidence attached to the journey.
body: Keep communications and documents linked to the business journey rather than scattered across channels.

sections.title: Match the pattern to the requirement.
body: Use APIs, events, real-time synchronization or batch according to the business requirement and source-system capability.

sections.title: Regional variation without a rewrite.
body: Configuration can support regional variation without implying every regulatory requirement is solved automatically.

sections.title: Controls that travel with the capability.
Make failures visible and recoverable.
body: The foundation should make failures visible and recoverable, not only optimize the happy path.

sections.title: Add new journeys without rebuilding everything underneath.
body: Modern interfaces and services can be introduced around existing systems first. Higher-change components can move out gradually. Core replacement can happen later where business value justifies it.

sections.title: Place automation and intelligence between experience and enterprise services.
body: Automation and intelligence sit between the experience layer and the enterprise services beneath it.
sections.note: Use rules and workflow for deterministic behaviour, and AI or model services only when interpretation, prediction or generation is required.

cta.title: Build a modern insurance layer around enterprise reality.

meta.title: Insurance Integrations | Core, Payments, Identity, Data & Partner APIs
meta.description: Connect insurance products with policy, CRM, claims, payments, identity, documents, data, communication and partner systems through appropriate integration patterns.

hero.title: Connect insurance without creating another silo.
hero.lede: A new digital product creates little value if teams still re-key information into the systems that run policy, claims, payments and customer operations. Iorta TechNXT integration work is designed around the business transaction: what information is needed, which system owns it, how quickly it must move and what should happen when a dependency is unavailable.

sections.title: Reach the systems that run the business.
body: Integration can expose or synchronize the capability required by SalesVerse, BrokerVerse, AgentVerse, CustomerVerse, MerchantVerse or ClaimVerse.
tags: Commission and finance systems where applicable

sections.title: One source of truth for who someone is.
body: Use the enterprise identity provider as the source of truth where appropriate instead of recreating identity inside every product.

sections.title: Connect money movement to the journey.
body: Payment providers and compliance requirements differ by market, so specific providers are named only where supported.

sections.title: Keep the paperwork inside the process.
tags: OCR and document processing where implemented

sections.title: Reach the customer the way they agreed to.
body: Communication should follow consent, preference and security requirements.

sections.title: Move information to where it gets used.
The organizations outside your walls.
Use the pattern that fits the transaction.

roles.description: When the caller needs an immediate response.
When selected state changes must remain closely aligned.
When source limitations or business timing make scheduled exchange appropriate.
When an external dependency is unavailable and the business cannot stop completely.

sections.title: Share on the customer's terms.
body: Open Finance and consent-based integration should follow the relevant market and institutional framework rather than being presented as one global standard.

sections.title: Build for the day the dependency is down.
Know which journey is affected, not just which service is down.
Automation needs transactions. Intelligence needs governed data.
body: Automation needs reliable transactional connectivity. Intelligent functions additionally need governed access to approved data, documents, knowledge and model services.

Potential integration areas include enterprise knowledge sources, document-intelligence services, model and LLM services where approved, data platforms, search and vector services where used, risk and fraud services, and communication channels.
sections.note: Sensitive core data is not exposed directly to external AI services without approved architecture and controls.

cta.title: Make integration reusable, observable and owned.

meta.title: Insurance Trust, Security & Operational Resilience | Iorta TechNXT
meta.description: Understand Iorta TechNXT's approach to access controls, secure engineering, auditability, responsible automation, monitoring and operational resilience.

hero.title: Trust built into the technology.
hero.lede: Insurance technology handles customer identity, financial information, policy data and business-critical operations. Buyers need more than a security paragraph: they need to understand how access, change, automation and operational failure are controlled.

sections.title: Access should reflect responsibility.
body: Access should reflect role and business responsibility rather than one broad internal-user permission.

sections.title: Security inside engineering, not after it.
Protect the data and say only what is documented.
body: Specific hosting, residency and retention commitments are published only when formally documented.
tags: Encryption in transit and at rest where implemented

sections.title: Reconstruct what happened.
body: Audit history should help operations and compliance teams reconstruct important business actions.

sections.title: Automate with accountability.
body: For intelligent and AI-supported functions, the level of control should increase with the impact of the decision.

sections.title: Controls in the pipeline.
Degrade predictably.
body: The application should degrade predictably when a dependent service is unavailable rather than leave business transactions in an unknown state.

sections.title: See the user impact, not only the alert.
Know what can interrupt the journey.
body: Maintain visibility into the dependencies that can interrupt a customer or operational journey.

sections.title: This page should become a Trust Center.
body: As verified material becomes available, this page will publish a security overview, privacy practices, responsible automation principles, data-processing information, subprocessor information where applicable, the business-continuity approach, a security contact, responsible disclosure and an architecture and security FAQ.
Certifications and attestations will appear only when actually held.

sections.title: No assurance without evidence.
body: We do not publish unsupported certifications, guaranteed uptime, recovery objectives, hosting regions, data-residency commitments, penetration-test results or regulatory compliance statements.

sections.title: Separate automation controls from AI controls.

features.description: Rule ownership, approval paths, permissions, exception handling, audit, rollback and workflow monitoring.
Approved purpose, data boundary, evaluation, human review, source and reference visibility where possible, override, monitoring, model and service change governance, and escalation.

sections.note: This distinction avoids over-governing simple rules while under-governing higher-risk AI behaviour.

cta.title: Move faster without giving up control.

meta.title: Insurance Software Implementation & Customer Success | Iorta TechNXT
meta.description: Move from insurance business challenge to production through discovery, design, configuration, integration, testing, launch, adoption and continuous improvement.

hero.title: From business challenge to production.
hero.lede: Enterprise insurance products do not succeed because the software is installed. They succeed when the business journey is clear, required systems are connected, users adopt the new way of working and operations can support it after go-live.

sections.title: Confirm what should change and what should stay.
body: Confirm what should change and what should remain before solution design begins.

sections.title: Agree the measure before the build.
body: Define measurable outcomes such as turnaround, adoption, workload or change speed where baselines are available.

sections.title: Validate assumptions before they become code.
body: Use prototypes and journey walkthroughs to validate important assumptions early.

sections.title: Keep standard, configured and bespoke visible.
body: Keep custom work explicit so the customer understands what is standard, what is configured and what is bespoke.

sections.title: Test the failure path too.
body: Test failure paths as well as successful transactions.

sections.title: Prove it against the real journey.
Only migrate what has to move.
body: Not every implementation requires data migration. Avoid adding it when system-of-record data remains in the existing platform.

sections.title: Go live with support already in place.
A working deployment is not yet a working change.
body: A technically successful deployment can still fail if teams continue using the old spreadsheet or email process.

sections.title: Keep changing after go-live.
What we watch after launch.
